decisions.rationale: Lead Archaludon and Pelipper to set Rain on turn 1, enabling instant Electro Shot and high-powered Rain attacks. Mega Swampert in the back acts as a powerful Swift Swim win condition, while Scarf Tsareena provides high Speed, Grass coverage, and Queenly Majesty protection against priority.
decisions.notebook:
Opponent Revealed Moves & Items:
- Mega Venusaur (Modest): Giga Drain, Sludge Bomb, Earth Power, Protect.
- Dedenne (Timid): Thunderbolt, Nuzzle, Volt Switch, Dazzling Gleam (Oran Berry, Cheek Pouch).
- Sneasler (Jolly): Close Combat, Poison Jab, Rock Slide, Protect (Focus Sash, Unburden).
- Farigiraf (Sassy): Trick Room, Psychic, Dazzling Gleam, Helping Hand (Mental Herb, Armor Tail).
- Benched: Incineroar, Gardevoir.

Strategic Plan:
- Rain setup with Pelipper empowers Archaludon's Electro Shot (+1 SpA per turn) and Hurricane.
- Mega Swampert sweeps under Swift Swim once opposing Grass threats (Mega Venusaur) are removed or softened.
- Choice Scarf Tsareena outspeeds baseline threats and blocks Fake Out / priority with Queenly Majesty.

decisions.rationale: Bring Trick Room (Farigiraf) to flip speed vs Pelipper Tailwind/Swift Swim/Scarf Tsareena, with Incineroar Fake Out/Intimidate to disrupt the Pelipper+Archaludon open. Venusaur-Mega (Thick Fat) handles Swampert/Garganacl via Giga Drain and Archaludon via Earth Power; Sneasler adds Close Combat/Rock Slide coverage. Gardevoir/Dedenne are too frail vs this physical rain core.
decisions.notebook: Opponent is a rain team: Pelipper (Drizzle, Focus Sash, Tailwind) + Archaludon (Leftovers/Stamina; Electro Shot charges in one turn under rain with +1 SpA; Draco Meteor) core. Tsareena is Choice Scarf, Queenly Majesty blocks our priority, outspeeds Sneasler; Sneasler's Focus Sash won't break on resisted Power Whip so no Unburden vs it. Farigiraf survives one Tsareena Power Whip and must set Trick Room before attacking. 4th slot among Swampert-Mega (Swift Swim), Garganacl (Salt Cure), Mimikyu (Disguise, has its own Trick Room). Plan: Venusaur-Mega (Thick Fat; Giga Drain for Swampert/Garganacl, Earth Power for Archaludon), Incineroar (Intimidate/Fake Out/Will-O-Wisp/Parting Shot), Farigiraf (Trick Room speed control), Sneasler (Close Combat for Archaludon/Garganacl, Rock Slide for Pelipper/Tsareena). Set Trick Room to flip speed vs Tailwind/Swift Swim/Scarf; Venusaur-Mega (80) and Incineroar (80) outpace Archaludon/Pelipper under Trick Room. Watch Mimikyu's own Trick Room and Tsareena's Queenly Majesty blocking Fake Out/priority.

decisions.rationale: Weather Ball into Incineroar takes advantage of Rain for 87.1-191.8% damage (likely KOing the primary disruptor). Electro Shot executes in one turn in Rain, granting Archaludon +1 SpA while chunking Farigiraf for 47.1-106.2% before potential Trick Room setup.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Incineroar)
decisions.rationale: Set Trick Room with Farigiraf to flip speed vs Pelipper/Archaludon (and future Swift Swim/Scarf). Neither Draco Meteor (38-55%) nor Hurricane (25-40%) can KO Farigiraf this turn, so Trick Room goes up safely. Incineroar Fake Out flinches Pelipper (priority +3, guaranteed first) to stop Tailwind/Hurricane this turn; Archaludon's Electro Shot only charges, and under Trick Room it fires last next turn. Keep Intimidate on field.

Tsareena Choice Scarf Queenly Majesty blocks our priority and outspeeds Sneasler; Sneasler's Focus Sash won't break on resisted Power Whip so no Unburden vs it. Farigiraf survives one Draco Meteor (38-55%) and Hurricane (25-40%). 4th slot among Swampert-Mega (Swift Swim), Garganacl (Salt Cure), Mimikyu (Disguise, own Trick Room). Farigiraf Armor Tail blocks all opposing priority moves.

decisions.rationale: Under Trick Room, Archaludon uses Rain-boosted Electro Shot into Farigiraf, gaining an instant +1 SpA boost to guarantee the KO on Farigiraf (62-141% damage at +2 SpA). Pelipper uses Rain-boosted Weather Ball into Incineroar for 87.1-191.8% super-effective damage, threatening a KO or severe damage on any switch-in.

Parting Shot Archaludon to drop its SpA from +1 to +0: at +1 its Electro Shot can KO Farigiraf (50% HP), but at +0 it only does 21-43% so Farigiraf survives. This also switches Incineroar out of Pelipper's rain WeatherBall (80-146%, possible OHKO); Venusaur takes it at 0.5x (14-48%). Farigiraf chips both foes with Dazzling Gleam.

Key: Pelipper's rain WeatherBall can OHKO Incineroar, so keep Incineroar off that slot; Venusaur takes it at 0.5x. Archaludon Electro Shot at +0 SpA is survivable for Farigiraf (21-43%); at +1 it threatens KO. Farigiraf ArmorTail blocks opposing priority. TR flips speed vs Tailwind/SwiftSwim/Scarf; Venusaur-Mega and Incineroar (80) outpace Archaludon/Pelipper under TR. Watch Mimikyu's own TR and Tsareena's QueenlyMajesty.

decisions.rationale: Forced to reposition Incineroar (threatened by rain WeatherBall). Venusaur-Mega is the safer switch: Thick Fat + Grass typing resists rain Water (0.5x) and it's more durable vs Pelipper Hurricane (36-121%) than Sneasler (48-170%), plus it threatens Archaludon with Earth Power and the backline with Giga Drain. Sneasler is poorly suited under Trick Room (fast = moves last, frail). Farigiraf passes; TR already up so losing it is acceptable.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 (down 0-1): Opponent rain core Pelipper (Drizzle/FocusSash; Hurricane 100% acc in rain, WeatherBall, Tailwind, WideGuard) + Archaludon (Leftovers/Stamina; Electro Shot charged+released turn2, Draco, FlashCannon). 2 unrevealed from Swampert-Mega(SwiftSwim)/Tsareena(Scarf/QueenlyMajesty)/Garganacl(SaltCure)/Mimikyu(own TR). TR up 4 turns, rain up 4. Plan: Venusaur-Mega (Thick Fat) handles Swampert/Garganacl via Giga Drain, Archaludon via Earth Power; resists rain Water. Sneasler (FocusSash/Unburden) is bad under TR (fast=last) - keep benched until TR expires or vs Tsareena/Pelipper with RockSlide. Incineroar Intimidate/FakeOut/Wisp/PartingShot for pivoting. Farigiraf ArmorTail blocks opposing priority; if it faints, watch Tsareena/Mimikyu priority. Watch Mimikyu's own TR and Tsareena QueenlyMajesty blocking our priority.

decisions.rationale: Farigiraf fainted, must bring a replacement. Under Trick Room, Incineroar (Speed 80) acts before both foes, while Sneasler (189) would move last—so Incineroar is the correct pivot, re-triggering Intimidate and enabling Fake Out/Parting Shot/Wisp. Venusaur has no legal action beyond Pass this turn; it resists Archaludon's charging Electro Shot and Pelipper's rain Water Ball, so staying in is safe.

decisions.rationale: Switching Pelipper to Tsareena brings Queenly Majesty onto the field, completely shutting down Incineroar's Fake Out. Using Protect on Archaludon safely blocks Venusaur's super-effective Earth Power and any targeting from Incineroar while gaining Leftovers healing. This positions Archaludon and Tsareena on Turn 4 to freely eliminate Venusaur with Draco Meteor and pressure Incineroar without taking damage this turn.

Tsareena uses High Jump Kick into Incineroar for 59.4-107.1% damage, putting heavy pressure on the slot while Queenly Majesty continues to neutralize priority moves.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

In Trick Room, Archaludon (105) outspeeds Sneasler (154-189). Active rain allows Electro Shot to execute instantly on Turn 5, boosting SpA and breaking Sneasler's Focus Sash. Tsareena uses super-effective High Jump Kick on Incineroar, which lacks Protect. As Trick Room expires after this turn, popping Sneasler's Sash guarantees our faster Choice Scarf Tsareena (204) and Swift Swim Mega Swampert can safely clean up on turn 6.

reflections.summary: The series and Game 2 were won through superior offensive rain pressure and anti-priority positioning. Relying on Archaludon under Rain overwhelmed Farigiraf's Trick Room setup and Mega Venusaur, while bringing Tsareena in Game 2 completely neutralized Incineroar's Fake Out disruption via Queenly Majesty. Not relying on Mega Swampert was correct, as Swampert would have struggled against Mega Venusaur, making Archaludon the ideal rain win condition. Leaving behind Galarian Slowking and Armarouge during series prep was justified given how cleanly Archaludon, Pelipper, and Tsareena dismantled the opponent's control tools.
reflections.adjustment: In a future rematch, maintain the Archaludon + Pelipper + Tsareena composition as the primary gameplan against their Farigiraf/Incineroar core. Consider bringing Mimikyu or Garganacl as back up over Swampert if Mega Venusaur is brought, as Swampert offers little leverage against Grass-type mega evolution while Archaludon handles Grass and Ground coverage effortlessly.
reflections.notebook:
Opponent Tendencies & Sets:
- Incineroar (Adamant, Sitrus Berry, Intimidate): Fake Out, Parting Shot, Flare Blitz, Will-O-Wisp. Relies on Fake Out to secure Trick Room.
- Farigiraf (Sassy, Mental Herb, Armor Tail): Trick Room, Psychic, Dazzling Gleam, Helping Hand.
- Mega Venusaur (Modest, Venusaurite): Giga Drain, Sludge Bomb, Earth Power, Protect.
- Sneasler (Jolly, Focus Sash): Close Combat, Poison Jab, Rock Slide, Protect.
- Gardevoir (Modest, Gardevoirite) & Dedenne (Timid, Oran Berry): Revealed in roster/earlier games.

Strategic Takeaways:
- Tsareena's Queenly Majesty hard-counters their Fake Out / priority utility, creating free setup turns for Archaludon.
- Archaludon under Rain (Electro Shot SpA boosts) reliably punches through both Trick Room setters and Mega Venusaur.
- Mega Swampert should be benched whenever Mega Venusaur is expected.

reflections.summary: Lost because the opponent's rain core (Pelipper + Archaludon) was never disrupted. Our lead of Incineroar + Farigiraf was too passive: Farigiraf got KO'd by a charged Electro Shot before Trick Room could pay off, and Venusaur-Mega was picked off by Draco Meteor. Tsareena's Queenly Majesty blocked Fake Out, and Pelipper's WideGuard neutralized Sneasler's Rock Slide when it finally came in. We never removed Pelipper early, so it kept enabling Archaludon and later finished Sneasler with Hurricane. The series was lost 0-2 because our game plan relied on a single Rock Slide that was both delayed and countered.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, bring a dedicated Pelipper answer that bypasses WideGuard and Queenly Majesty. Lead with Sneasler + Dedenne: Dedenne's Thunderbolt is super effective and outspeeds Pelipper, while Sneasler can target Archaludon with Close Combat. Alternatively, use Incineroar's Parting Shot to pivot into a faster threat, but avoid relying on Fake Out. Consider swapping Venusaur-Mega for Gardevoir-Mega or Dedenne in the four brought, and keep Farigiraf alive longer by protecting it or using a bulkier lead. If Trick Room is the plan, pair it with a redirector or protect Farigiraf on turn 1.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's rain core: Pelipper (Focus Sash, WideGuard, Hurricane, Weather Ball, Tailwind) + Archaludon (Stamina, Leftovers, Electro Shot charge+release, Draco Meteor). Tsareena (Choice Scarf, Queenly Majesty, HJK, Power Whip, Triple Axel, U-turn). 4th likely Swampert-Mega (Swift Swim) or Garganacl or Mimikyu. Key tendencies: Pelipper uses WideGuard to block spread moves; Tsareena blocks Fake Out; Archaludon boosts SpA with Electro Shot and gains Defense from Stamina. Need to remove Pelipper early with a single-target super effective move (Electric or Rock) that isn't spread. Physical attackers should avoid Archaludon unless using Fighting/Ground moves. Trick Room is viable but must protect Farigiraf from Electro Shot. Queenly Majesty forces us to avoid Fake Out leads. Prep: bring Dedenne or another fast Electric attacker; consider Gardevoir for speed control and special coverage. Leave Venusaur-Mega only if it can survive Draco Meteor or be saved for late game.
